**Owner rule for every session and agent (2026-11-12): tests must truly check functionality. No "green for the sake of green".**

It's in CLAUDE.md once PR #108 merges, and it applies now:
- Every new or changed test must **fail without the code**. Revert or break the logic and watch it go red before you push. Say in the PR which mutation you tried.
- Assert **outcomes** a driver would notice: the route chosen, the switch made or refused, the spoken line, the request count. Don't assert mock calls, "something rendered", or snapshots nobody reads.
- **Never weaken a test to get green.** No loosened assertions, wider tolerances, retries, or `skip`/`only`/`todo`. If a test is wrong, say why and replace it with one that checks the same behaviour.
- **A flaky test is a bug.** Find the race. Don't rerun until green.
- Reviewers will block PRs whose tests wouldn't catch their own bug.

— orchestrator

Phone build: shell-ios run **43209431280** (green, `RouteIQ-unsigned`, head 390490f): `gh run download 43209431280 -R akashdesai93/routeiq -n RouteIQ-unsigned -D $HOME\dev\routeiq-builds\diag136-43209431280`. ## What is in it (all reachable only in lab mode)

- **Native switches** `-routeiqLabSwitch a,b` (RouteIQLab.swift; read only when `-routeiqLab <scenario>` is there too, gate pinned by `tests/labBlackScreen.test.ts` and `native/shell/tests/shell.test.mjs`): turn off one start-of-drive action each (`no-idle`, `no-audio`, `no-speech`, `no-bglocation`, `no-location`, `no-always`, `no-testdrive`); remedies (`kick-layout|display|scroll|frame|opaque|readd` at 0.5/2/5 s after Start and on becoming active, `audio-offmain`, `insets-never`); probes (`marks`: window cyan / web view magenta / scroll view green; `snapshot`: `takeSnapshot` 3/9/18 s in).
- **Always-on native probe in lab mode** (`RouteIQLabView.swift`, plugin method `labNative`, the report's `native` line): main-thread stalls ≥ 100 ms with their time since Start drive, web content process ended (a navigation-delegate proxy that hands everything on to Capacitor's), web view in window / hidden / opaque / colours / layer in tree, scroll view frame / offset / content size / insets / adjusted insets / behaviour, window safe area, app state events.
- **Web side**: `--early nomap|red|rednomap` (changed before Start drive), `--fix kick-<name>` and `--fix snapshot` (native, 12 s in, on a screen that is already black), the report written the moment Start drive is pressed.
- **`drive-screen` now measures seconds from Start drive until drawn**: screenshots one after another for up to 40 s, `drawn.json` with each one's time, flatness and commonest colour; passes only when drawn **≤ 2 s and still drawn** (`DEFAULT_LAB_CHECKS.maxDrawnSec`). `syslog.txt` now also keeps the WebKit GPU and web content processes' errors and exits.
- **Guard for afterwards**: `queue.mjs` refuses a build whose runs leave out `drive-screen` (unless `"noDriveScreen"` says why); docs/phone-lab.md says every build touching `native/shell`, the drive view or the map gets it, 5 starts in a row.

Outside lab mode nothing changes: the engine's switch set is `RouteIQLab.active`, empty without the lab argument; the monitor is created only after the lab check; its three methods reject without it.

## Hypotheses, ranked (from the code; no phone here)

What happens natively at Start drive, all on the **main thread** (`RouteIQEngine`): `startLocation` → `begin()` sets `allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates`/`showsBackgroundLocationIndicator`, `startUpdatingLocation()`, once ever `requestAlwaysAuthorization()`, starts the 1 s tick; `startSimulatedRoute` starts the test-drive timer; `keepAwake(true)` sets `isIdleTimerDisabled`; the first spoken line calls `AVAudioSession.setCategory(.playback, .voicePrompt, …)` + `setActive(true)` **synchronously on the main thread**, then `AVSpeechSynthesizer.speak`. Nothing native touches the web view, its frame, insets or opacity. Capacitor itself (8.6, `CAPBridgeViewController.prepareWebView`) gives the web view `UIColor.systemBackground` (black in Dark Mode), the window has no colour (black), and `ios.contentInset: "always"` makes the scroll view add the safe area to its insets.

| # | Hypothesis | For | Against / unknown | Decided by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **H1** | **WebKit stops presenting its layer tree** (remote layer tree frozen or its visible/unobscured rect stale) after something at Start drive changes the app's activity state or the scroll view's geometry; a foreground cycle re-sends activity state and visible rects and it draws. Triggers to separate: a resign/become-active pair (system prompt, e.g. the one-time "Always" upgrade), the scroll view's offset/insets under `contentInset: "always"`. | Page alive in script but nothing on the glass, plain DOM black too, foreground cures it, old build too. WebKit has had exactly this class ("WKWebView can get stuck blank: Web Content process thinks the app is backgrounded", [bug 203774](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=203774)). | The trigger is unknown. | `marks` (magenta = web view there, its content not presented), `native` events (inactive/active around Start), kicks curing a black screen at 12 s, `no-always`, `insets-never` |
| **H2** | **The GPU process** (it renders WebGL and, on iOS 17+, the page's DOM layers too) **crashes, is jetsammed or stalls** when the drive view's map canvas grows (440x676 at 3x, new drive layers) and the web view shows nothing until it is re-composited. | Plain DOM black as well as the map; both old and new builds have the map in the drive view; "drew by itself at 18 s" fits a relaunched GPU process; foreground fixes it. Related reports: WebGL canvas lost or frozen in WKWebView ([Apple forum 688784](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/688784), [Textastic](`` https://feedback.textasticapp.com/communities/1/topics/4001-webgl2-graphics-context-is-sometimes-lost-in-the-built-in-html-viewer-after-backgrounding-the-app), `` [GPU process crash on iOS 26.4](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/822200)). | PR #141's WebGL-loss rebuild did not help, but it only fires on `webglcontextlost`. | `--early nomap` (never black ⇒ the map is the trigger), `syslog.txt` (GPU process exit/jetsam lines, now collected), `webglcontextlost` in the history |
| **H3** | **Main-thread stall at Start**: the audio session activation, a synchronous call to the audio daemon on our main thread, reported to block the UI for 0.5 s ([cocoa-dev 2018](https://lists.apple.com/archives/cocoa-dev/2018/Nov/msg00033.html)) up to tens of seconds ([Apple forum 853278](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/853278)) and usually moved off the main thread ([Apple forum 697861](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/697861)), CLLocationManager start or the Always prompt hold the main thread while WebKit swaps in the drive view's layers. | Exactly the kind of multi-second delay seen; the first line ("RouteIQ started") is spoken at Start. | A stall alone would freeze the plan screen, not paint black; 18 s is long for a stall. | `native` line: `longestSinceDriveMs`; `no-speech`, `no-audio`, `audio-offmain` |
| H4 | **The black band (860 of 956 points)** is `contentInset: "always"`: 956 − 62 (top safe area) − 34 (bottom) = 860, exactly the page height measured. Separate defect, certain cause; maybe also feeds H1. | The arithmetic. | Whether it also causes the black screen. | `insets-never`: page 956 tall, `adjustedInset` 0, band gone |
| H5 | Background location flags set while in front / location start. | Changed in the same moment. | No known reports. | `no-bglocation`, `no-location` |
| H6 | Idle timer (`isIdleTimerDisabled`). | Same moment. | No known reports; it is a flag. | `no-idle` |

pulls.body:
Refs #98 (PR 2 of the battery work: standing still). Independent of #151; either can merge first.

## What changes
- `RouteIQStillness.swift` (new, pure Swift, Foundation only) decides which GPS fixes and native ticks cross into the web view.
  - **Standing still**: once the car has stood still for 10 s (under 0.5 m/s, within 25 m of where it stopped), a fix goes through only every 3 s, and a tick only when nothing went for 3 s.
  - **Moving**: every fix goes through. No native tick is sent while fixes flow, because they are the web app's clock already. If fixes stop for 1.5 s (a tunnel), the ticks come back every second.
  - **Resume**: the first fix that moves passes at once. Moving means 0.5 m/s or more, more than 25 m from the stop, or speed unknown.
  - Thresholds live in `RouteIQStillness.defaultOptions`.
- `RouteIQEngine.swift`: the GPS fixes and the test drive's made-up fixes both go through `forward()`, so a scripted stop tries the hold at home. The heartbeat asks `stillness.tick`. The gate is reset at `begin()` and at the start of a test drive.
- **Core Location is not touched.** `BestForNavigation`, `kCLDistanceFilterNone`, `.automotiveNavigation` and `pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically = false` stay exactly as they were. `native/shell/tests/shell.test.mjs` now fails if any of them changes. A planted `distanceFilter = 10` turns it red.

## Why this cannot let iOS suspend the app
iOS keeps an app with a background location session running while Core Location delivers updates to it. Nothing on the `CLLocationManager` changes. Updates keep arriving in Swift at about 1 Hz while parked; the hold only decides which of them are passed into the web view. A `distanceFilter` or `pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically` would stop those deliveries while parked, and that is how a background app gets suspended. Neither is used.

## Numbers (from the rules, not from a phone)
| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 minutes parked: fixes into the web view | 600 | 206 (every one for the first 10 s, then one every 3 s) |
| 10 minutes parked: native ticks into the web view | 600 | 0 extra (the kept fixes are the clock) |
| Driving: native ticks into the web view | 1 a second | 0 while fixes flow; every second again 1.5 s after they stop |
| Delay of the first fix after moving off | none | none (passed on at once) |

None of this is measured on a phone. Battery and CPU effects are unknown until the phone checks below are run.

## How it was verified
- `bash native/shell/scripts/test-swift-logic.sh` (new; runs on Linux and macOS; added to `shell-ios.yml`) covers:
  - 10 minutes parked
  - drift within 20 m
  - resume by speed, by distance, and with unknown speed
  - creeping at 0.6 m/s
  - ticks not using up the fix's turn
  - GPS lost while parked: ticks every 3 s, with an upper bound
  - a tunnel while moving: ticks back at 1.5 s, then every second
  - the clock stepping back, for fixes and ticks
  - reset
- `tests/stillness.test.ts` drives the same stop twice through the web live engine: once with every fix, once with the thinned stream.
  - Same spoken lines.
  - The checks of the first two minutes of the stop: as many, each at most 3 s late.
  - Every second from 200 s to 400 s the gate reads `stationary`, never `no-fix`.
  - The first check after moving off comes in the same second.
  - The Swift defaults are read from the Swift source and checked against the web's `maxFixAgeSec` and the diagnostics' `TICK_GAP_EVENT_MS`.
  - A 20-minute parked run through `createDriveDiagnostics` logs no `no tick for` or `no fix for` line.
- typecheck, lint, `npx vitest run` (824), shell `npm test` (23), `npm run e2e` (39; no web code changed).
- Mutations tried, each caught:
  - keep-alive counted from any event
  - no resume by distance
  - unknown speed treated as still
  - hold from the first still fix
  - moving not ending the hold
  - event time kept only for fixes (garage ticks every second)
  - no clock-back guard on fixes
  - no tick drop while moving
  - tick quiet period of 5 s
  - `keepAliveSec: 12` (the web gate reads `no-fix`)
  - `keepAliveSec: 5` (false "no tick for 5 s" lines in diagnostics, and over the guard)
  - `distanceFilter = 10` (shell test)
- The route-logic-reviewer agent ran before the commit, with these results:
  - **Its blocking finding**: a 5 s keep-alive would log a false `no tick for 5 s` on nearly every parked event and push real events out of the 200-line log. That is why the keep-alive is 3 s now, with guards.
  - **Also fixed**: two mutations that survived, the bound used against the 10 s fix age, a reset at the start of a test drive, and PLAN.md.

- `native/shell/tests/shell.test.mjs` also changes in #113 (phone lab). Expect a small merge in the file list line.

3. Test drive with a stop in its script (or a real red light longer than 10 s): the car is seen moving again at once.
4. Locked wrong-turn lab scenario (#113): still passes.
5. Battery: 30 minutes parked with a drive running, locked, off the charger, compared with `main` (battery % and the iOS Battery screen's share for RouteIQ). Same for 30 minutes of driving.
